messages:
maria-ops: Heads up — EU edge cluster (eu1) getting a steady stream of customer reports: p95 generation latency up from ~120ms to ~620ms since 02:15 UTC, and a few 401s during spikes. A single enterprise customer opened a support ticket and attached curl traces.
jonathan-sre: A few questions — did anything roll in eu1 around that window? driver/kernel/firmware?
maria-ops: We rolled the host kernel security patch at 01:50 UTC, and a GPU firmware push landed in the eu1-dedicated pool at 01:40 UTC. deploy-bot: deploy eu1/kf-firmware v3.2.1 -> success @ 01:40:12 UTC :white_check_mark:
lee-eng: Reproduced a p95 jump locally on a small repro. When background io pushes to hostfs, token fetch (auth) latencies climb and we see 401s from auth when timeout crosses 800ms. Looks like upstream token verification times out.
nana-cs: Customer says 401s show up in their app logs during retries — makes the UX worse. Ticket number CS-8993.
jonathan-sre: Can we get kernel dmesg + iostat from an affected host? Also check nvme queues. I ran a quick check on one node:
jonathan-sre: ```
> iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  %util
nvme0n1         12.00   34.00  1024.0  2048.0   0.00   0.00  87.5
```
lee-eng: And kube-proxy logs show repeated 504s for auth-service during the spike window. Sample from proxy: `W backend response timeout after 800ms`
maria-ops: Support-bot forwarded the customer's curl trace: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` then `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error=\"invalid_token\"` — but that could be caused by token server timeouts, not token validity.
jonathan-sre: Hypothesis: GPU firmware push increased hostfs/io contention (nvme qdepth shift) -> higher CPU scheduling latency on the node -> auth token fetch timeout -> application returns 401 or 504 to clients -> perceived p95/p99 spike.
lee-eng: Repro steps I used:
lee-eng: 1) Run stress-ng io --hdd 4 on a worker with kvcache enabled
lee-eng: 2) Fire 1k short-lived inference requests (freya) from a load generator
lee-eng: 3) Observe auth latencies: token fetch 95p goes from 60ms -> 900ms and we start seeing 401s
ana-cs: Customer repro attached similar curl loop and timestamps align with our probe.
jonathan-sre: Mitigation plan:
jonathan-sre: - Immediate: add routing fallback for eu1 to eu2 for enterprise customers (canary) to reduce user impact. I'll open a route rollback ticket.
jonathan-sre: - Short term: throttle background firmware rollout for remaining hosts, pause next batch.
jonathan-sre: - Mid term: revert kernel security patch on one suspect host and monitor.
lee-eng: Also going to push a temporary increase of auth-service request timeout from 800ms -> 2000ms to reduce 401s during transient IO noise (risk: longer tail for real failures).
maria-ops: Can infra ops pause the remaining firmware batch? deploy-bot: rollback scheduled for eu1 firmware batch -> paused by @maria-ops @ 02:38 UTC :stop_sign:
support-bot: Noted — opened incident INC-2026 and attached CS-8993.
jonathan-sre: I'll collect perf counters (iostat, nvme-cli, top -H, perf sched) and post a short triage snippet in 10m. If we see sustained %util > 85% on nvme with high latency, that's root cause.
lee-eng: Quick tweak applied: increased auth timeout on canary edge pool (eu2) and enabled routing fallback for 20% of enterprise traffic. Monitoring: showing reduced 401s for redirected traffic.
nana-cs: Customer updated ticket — they see improvement when we routed to eu2, but still intermittents on eu1. They appreciated the quick fallback. :pray:
maria-ops: Next actions: jonathan — collect logs and attach to INC-2026. lee — prepare rollback playbook for kernel/firmware if perf counters correlate. ana — keep CS updated and offer temporary workspace migration guide.
jonathan-sre: Collected logs (snippet):
jonathan-sre: ```
[02:16:24] nvme error: io latency 4.5ms (avg) dev nvme0n1
[02:16:24] cpu sched: avg latency 210us -> 1.2ms
[02:16:25] auth-proxy: downstream request timeout after 800ms
```
jonathan-sre: Early signal: nvme qdepth shifted after firmware push on host-57, correlates with spike. I'll start bisecting hosts in the batch.
lee-eng: I'll prepare a lightweight fix: reduce kvcache write-behind aggressiveness on affected hosts to lower hostfs flush bursts. Rollout as config change ASAP.
maria-ops: Thanks all. Ana, keep customer notified with status + ETA for rollback if needed. We'll update INC-2026 in 30m or sooner if rollback starts. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
